newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: FOCUS-Ascom takes charge to wipe slate clean.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-Ascom takes charge to wipe slate clean.

text.p: Swiss telecoms group Ascom Holding AG on Wednesday reported a 1996 loss of 128 million francs ($87.3 million) after charges of 152 million to free itself of past problems and start with a clean slate.

Ascom, which has been struggling to adapt to liberalised telecommunications markets, also said it had sold a small U.S. development company, Nexion, and added that its troubled Timeplex unit had returned to profitability in the fourth quarter of 1996.
"Consciously we didn't want to burden the current year with problems left over from the past," Ascom chairman Felix Wittlin told a news conference.
Wittlin declined to specify how much of the restructuring charges would be spent on Nexion, but said they would cover various problem areas in both the United States and Europe.
He added the move was not taken to make Ascom more desirable for a merger or alliance with another company.
"The precautionary provisions were not taken to beautify us for a marriage," he said.

Ascom, the product of a 1987 merger of three traditional suppliers to Swiss PTT, ran into serious difficulties in 1993 but has gradually pulled itself from the danger zone by focusing on core activities and selling non-core businesses.
From a 1993 operating loss of 130 million francs and debt of almost one billion, Ascom reported a 1996 operating profit of 94 million -- up 25 percent from 1995 -- and a debt burden of 470 million.
The company has set targets to safeguard this recovery, including the goal that operating margins should reach five percent in 1998, from 1996's 3.2 percent.
"We want to remain a solid, successful company with an appropriate profit," said Wittlin.
The new strategy also calls for focusing on selected market segments in telecommuncations and service automation, mainly in Europe and in some southeast Asian markets.
Shareholders, however, will once again have to forego a dividend, despite expectations of a satisfactory 1997.
"Personally I am expecting a net profit but I cannot give you an estimate of its size," Wittlin said, adding Ascom was budgeting for a "decent operating result" in 1997.
Orders in the first quarter of 1997 were clearly ahead of last year, while revenue was slightly lower, Ascom said, without giving further details.
Ascom's board proposed waiving a dividend on 1996 results after resuming payment last year at 25 Swiss francs per bearer share, the first dividend in three years.
Orders last year fell 1.8 percent to 2.77 billion francs while sales were roughly steady at 2.94 billion.
The workforce fell by around 750 to 11,740, mainly due to a reduction of some 500 jobs at Timeplex, which supplies products and services to private telecommunications networks worldwide.

The sale of Nexion, a small development company with 180 people and no sales, to a large multinational firm was agreed on Tuesday, but Wittlin said the companies had agreed not to release details until the deal was sealed and approved.
In the first half of 1996 Ascom's Enterprise Networks segment, which consisted of Nexion and Timeplex, lost 39 million francs. ($ = 1.466 Swiss Francs)
